And this is my model specification in R:

model = 
'
       ### Latent variables

        F1 =~ V1 + V2 + V3 + V4
        F2 =~ V5 + V6 + V7
        F3 =~ V8 + V9 + V10 + V11

        F3 ~ F6 + F5 + F1
        F4 ~ F6 + F5 + F1

fit = sem(model, data = data, estimator = "MLR")
summary(fit)

I do not understand the mistake ...

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Help from EQS to R
parts:
different results ...
But i don't understand the reason

That's not very specific.  Are your parameter estimates within rounding error?  Note that EQS uses N − 1 in some computations where lavaan would use N by default (which you can switch using mimic="EQS" or setting likelihood = "wishart").  You can read the documentation on ?lavOptions and the EQS manual to see whether you are requesting the same robust SEs and test statistic from both programs.   You could show us something specific that differs by pasting that small part of each package's output.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.subject: Re: Help from EQS to R
parts:
EQS is the first SEM program I used ... but haven't used it for over two decades. Anyway, just a few observations that I hope can help.

- I believe you are right about model specifications. The model dfs are different, 159 in lavaan and 160 in EQS.
- The numbers of free disturbances are the same (4).
- The numbers of regression coefficients are the same (10).
- However, the numbers of error variances are different. 19 in lavaan but 20 in EQS. The error variance of V20 was fixed to zero in lavaan but free in EQS.
- The loadings of V1 and V20 are fixed to 1 in lavaan but free in EQS.
- I don't see the covariance between F1 and F6 in EQS. You did not explicitly ask for it in the model syntax of lavaan but they are free by default. Is it fixed to zero by default in EQS?
- I also don't see the covariances between the disturbances of F2, F3, and F4 in EQS (there are three), while they are free in lavaan (added by default, I believe). Maybe they are also fixed to zero by default in EQS?

Hope I did not read the EQS model wrong. You may check these issues first to make sure that the same model is fitted in both lavaan and EQS.

Hope this helps.

-- Shu Fai

parts:
This is what I do for similar cases in my work:

mod <- "F1 =~ @trigger@ * V1 + V2 + V3 + V4"

new_mod <- function(i) {
    gsub("@trigger@",
         i,
         mod,
         fixed = TRUE)
  }
new_mod(sample(c(0, 1), 1))
#> [1] "F1 =~ 1 * V1 + V2 + V3 + V4"
new_mod(sample(c(0, 1), 1))
#> [1] "F1 =~ 0 * V1 + V2 + V3 + V4"
new_mod(sample(c(0, 1), 1))
#> [1] "F1 =~ 1 * V1 + V2 + V3 + V4"
new_mod(sample(c(0, 1), 1))
#> [1] "F1 =~ 1 * V1 + V2 + V3 + V4"

You can name @trigger@ in any way you want. Just make sure that it does not conflict with other words in the model syntax when calling gsub().

Hope this helps.

Regards,
Shu Fai Cheung (張樹輝)

parts: Correction: I should have set the mode syntax as an argument. Coding it inside the function definition is fine for internal use, but is not a good practice. Passing the model syntax as an argument also allows us to change the model syntax without the need to redefine the function.
mod <- "F1 =~ @trigger@ * V1 + V2 + V3 + V4"

new_mod <- function(i, model) {
    gsub("@trigger@",
         i,
         model,
         fixed = TRUE)
  }
set.seed(87041)
new_mod(sample(c(0, 1), 1), model = mod)
#> [1] "F1 =~ 1 * V1 + V2 + V3 + V4"
new_mod(sample(c(0, 1), 1), model = mod)
#> [1] "F1 =~ 1 * V1 + V2 + V3 + V4"
new_mod(sample(c(0, 1), 1), model = mod)
#> [1] "F1 =~ 0 * V1 + V2 + V3 + V4"
new_mod(sample(c(0, 1), 1), model = mod)
#> [1] "F1 =~ 1 * V1 + V2 + V3 + V4"

Regards,
Shu Fai Cheung (張樹輝)
